questions.title: Which team will win the second Test of Pakistan's 2026 tour of the West Indies?
questions.background: Pakistan and the West Indies are scheduled to contest a two-match Test cricket series in the Caribbean.

local_articles.title: Back from the wilderness: Abdullah Shafique proves his class
local_articles.snippet: Dropped from the squad due to wretched form, Abdullah Shafique could not have made a more dramatic comeback to the Test arena. The classy Pakistan batter was an emergency replacement for Shan Masood, who suffered a finger injury during the first Test, which the West Indies won handsomely. Out of the Test team since October last year, Shafique grabbed the opportunity with both hands, scoring a brilliant century on the second day of the second Test in Port of Spain. Walking in at 34 for one, the opener needed to adapt to his new role as the number three after the West Indies made 344 in their first innings. But the right-hander rose to the challenge beautifully, pacing his innings with ease to register his sixth Test century (111 not out off 193 balls, 11 fours and two sixes). questions.current_reasoning: Election-eve Aug 1-3 polling and prediction-market consolidation ahead of tomorrow's Aug 4 primary (Newsweek Aug 1 & Aug 3, Kalshi News Aug 3): three additional late surveys all show commanding double-digit leads for Abdul El-Sayed — Mitchell Research & Communications (July 28-29, N=406 LV) at 52%-38% (+14), Zenith Research (July 26-30, N=536 LV) at 53%-34% initial and 59%-41% pushed (+18), and The Public Sentiment Institute (July 25-29, N=762) at 54.8%-45.2% allocated (+9.6, modeling a 96% win probability) — reinforcing Emerson (+15/+16) and Tavern (+11) with no recent poll favoring Stevens. On Monday morning Aug 3, both Kalshi and Polymarket rose to 97%-98% for El-Sayed. Nudging Abdul El-Sayed 0.91 -> 0.94 and trimming Haley Stevens 0.09 -> 0.06, retaining a 6% upset buffer below markets for older/absentee voter composition (65+ voters break 50%+ for Stevens) and the July 8-11 Glengariff outlier.

questions.background: Rodri is a midfielder for Manchester City.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from the clubs involved, corroborated by reliable sports reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the receiving club in Rodri's first completed permanent transfer from Manchester City during the 2026 summer transfer window. Transfer rumours, bids, and agreements in principle do not qualify. Resolution Date : The date the completed transfer is officially announced. Accepted Answer Format : The receiving club's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: July 31-Aug 3 updates (Fabrizio Romano via FootballTransfers, SI, Goal/Sky, Football Presse, Fichajes, RPP citing Cadena SER & AS): the rumored July 30 finalization did not happen, and talks between Real Madrid and Manchester City have stalled over a EUR 15m-25m valuation gap (City holding firm at EUR 70m-75m vs Madrid's EUR 50m-60m offers), with City boss Enzo Maresca dismissing links as 'just speculation' on Aug 1 and Rodri's back-surgery rehab reducing Madrid's urgency. Crucially, Cadena SER and AS reported on Aug 3 that Barcelona have actively re-entered the frame to cover Frenkie de Jong's multi-month knee MCL tear — noting Rodri likes Barcelona's project though Barca face LaLiga FFP constraints and a ~EUR 50m ceiling — while PSG, Atletico Madrid, and Bayern remain silent and Romano stresses Rodri's desire to return to Spain. Real Madrid remain clear favorites (agreed personal terms, Mourinho pressing, new ~EUR 65m proposal anticipated), but trimming Real Madrid 0.65 -> 0.61 on the fee impasse, promoting Barcelona to #2 (0.09 -> 0.16), and nudging Paris Saint-Germain 0.10 -> 0.08 and Atletico Madrid 0.08 -> 0.06 (Bayern 0.03, sum 0.94).

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 Republican primary for Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District?
questions.background: Andy Ogles has represented Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives since 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Tennessee election results, with a definitive Associated Press race call accepted before certification. Resolution Event : The determination of the winner of the Republican primary for Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District scheduled for August 6, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Fresh July 31 local reporting (TriStar Daily, Nashville Banner) strengthens the case for a near-tossup heading into Thursday's Aug 6 primary. Invest in Tomorrow Coalition shared cross-tabs of a larger N=1,046 likely GOP primary voter poll (MOE +/-3.3%) showing an even tighter initial dead heat—Andy Ogles 33.0% vs Charlie Hatcher 31.5% (35.5% undecided)—with Hatcher surging to a 44.9%-24.0% lead on the informed ballot as ITC deploys its $2.0M ad barrage (vs ~$500K-$666K for Freedom Caucus Fund). Early voting concluded Saturday Aug 1 across the drastically redrawn, Nashville-free rural/agricultural TN-5 map, and local analysts note Ogles' hurried July 28 Trump tele-rally may have had limited reach given Ogles' weak cash position ($58K vs Hatcher's $105K). Still keeping Ogles a modest favorite given Trump's endorsement in a Trump +23 seat, incumbency, PAC-poll lean, and his 2024 primary survival, trimming Andy Ogles 0.62 -> 0.56 and lifting Charlie Hatcher 0.38 -> 0.44.

local_articles.title: Florida primary early voting is underway; more than 566,000 ballots already cast statewide
local_articles.snippet: More than half a million votes have been cast for Florida's primary election as the "early voting" option opened in 10 counties on Monday. Just after noon on Tuesday, the Division of Elections reported just over 566,000 people voted by mail and 9,000 went to an "early voting" location. Bradford, Calhoun, Hendry, Hillsborough, Jefferson, Miami-Dade, Monroe, Orange, Putnam and Santa Rosa counties opened early voting locations on Monday. Supervisors in Hardee, Highlands, Lake, Levy and Nassau counties start the process on Thursday, followed by Alachua, Citrus, Duval and Osceola counties on Friday. From Saturday through Aug. 15, all 67 counties are required to offer the in-person voting option. questions.title: What source of cocaine exposure will UK Anti-Doping cite when publicly explaining the resolution of Joseph Parker's October 2025 doping case?
questions.background: Joseph Parker is a former world heavyweight boxing champion from New Zealand. He tested positive for cocaine in connection with his October 2025 fight against Fabio Wardley and has denied knowingly taking banned substances.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : UK Anti-Doping's official decision or public statement explaining the resolution of Parker's case arising from the cocaine tests associated with his October 2025 bout. Resolution : Resolve when UK Anti-Doping publicly identifies the source of Parker's cocaine exposure in its explanation of the case's resolution. Use the source identified by the agency. Accepted Answer Format : A concise noun phrase identifying the stated source of exposure.
questions.current_reasoning: Late June to July 8 updates (RNZ June 24, World Boxing News July 4, Seconds Out July 7, Boxing 24/7 July 8; no UKAD verdict announced as of July 30) provide key new clues from manager Spencer Brown's Playbook Boxing interview. Brown stated there were 'mitigating circumstances' involving 'the people around him at the time. There was contamination,' confirmed the defense submitted 'witness statements,' and remarked 'all we are waiting for is a yes, OK then accept it, there's your ban' (hoping to fight again in 2-3 months). Attributing contamination to 'the people around him at the time' backed by witness statements shifts probability sharply away from factory-contaminated supplements (rare for cocaine and reliant on batch testing rather than witness statements) and toward bystander/interpersonal exposure routes. Accordingly, lifting Contaminated drink 0.18 -> 0.22 (aligning with Parker's earlier 'cup of tea' remark and social/entourage contamination) and Environmental contamination 0.09 -> 0.14 (surfaces/banknotes/handling around users), nudging Out-of-competition recreational use 0.10 -> 0.12 (WADA Substance of Abuse fallback if UKAD deems contamination proof insufficient), holding Contaminated food near 0.10, and replacing Contaminated supplement (0.15) with Intimate contact at 0.08 (a well-established WADA/CAS cocaine-transfer route supported by witness statements), leaving 34% residual across narrower or alternative phrasings.
